summary: Baker County, OR cabin on a 7,873-ft summit, built 1934; register and firelookout.com say abandoned 1937, a 1938 newspaper item cites the lookout; now gone.

facts.status_note: Cabin abandoned in 1937 and gone, per the register; no source describes what remains

staffing.status: a 1938 newspaper item reports a fire from Bull Run Lookout; no other staffing details found

events.note: Cabin built on the site (register, firelookout.com)
Register and firelookout.com date abandonment to 1937; see resolved_conflicts
Lightning fire four miles south of the station reported from Bull Run Lookout (August 25, 1938 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Registered November 19, 2019 as US 1833, OR 556; nominated by Tammy McLeod

evidence.supports: cabin built on the site in 1934
evidence.quote: A cabin was built on the site in 1934.
It was abandoned in 1937 and is gone.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts places the site in the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
register places the site in the Malheur National Forest
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
lightning fire four miles south of the station reported from Bull Run Lookout
evidence.quote: Lightning caused a report to be sent in from Bull Run Lookout of a fire four miles south of that station Wednesday evening at 7:00.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1937. The Forest Lookouts page quotes an August 25, 1938 newspaper item that reports a fire from Bull Run Lookout. The sources do not reconcile the two, so the story reports both.

The register names the Malheur National Forest and the Forest Lookouts page names the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest. firelookout.com names both as Wallowa-Whitman/Malheur. The story gives both names.

notes_for_editor: Two conflicts are left open: the 1937 abandonment date vs the 1938 newspaper item, and the national forest name. The brief's status 'gone' stands. The west_us_lookouts crawl record reads 'Removed' and Wallowa-Whitman, which matches the Forest Lookouts page. The 2008 site photo was not viewable, so the story does not describe the site today. No access statement was found, so the access key is omitted. The brief's elevation (2,399.7 m) matches the register's 7,873 ft.
